summary: Multi-Topology Routing and Flexible Algorithm each create sub-topologies inside a network using different constraints. This document defines extensions to Multipoint LDP so it can be deployed in networks that use these or similar methods of signaling non-default topologies.

plainLanguage.summary: A city can have separate road maps for buses, bikes and trucks. This lets a method for delivering one stream to many viewers pick the right map each time.

how does mldp use flexible algorithm
subtitle: How multicast label-switched paths learn to follow a particular topology and IGP algorithm.

tldr.problem: Networks can run Multi-Topology Routing or Flexible Algorithm to build separate sub-topologies, but Multipoint LDP had no way to say which topology or algorithm a multipoint path should follow.
tldr.mechanism: The pair {MT-ID, IPA} is made part of the mLDP FEC by reusing the MT IP address families and turning 8 bits of a reserved field into an IPA field. A new MT Multipoint capability announces support, and upstream and downstream selection are restricted to the chosen sub-topology.
tldr.outcome: Multipoint LSPs can be built along a specific topology and algorithm. The document updates RFC 7307 and is a Proposed Standard.

facts.label: IPA field
facts.value: 8 bits, taken from the 16-bit Reserved field

today: RFC 9658 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2024. It updates RFC 7307 and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why mLDP Needs Topology Awareness
sections.content:
Multi-Topology Routing (MTR) lets an IP network keep several distinct topologies, each with its own routes. The IGPs (OSPF and IS-IS) and LDP were already extended for it, and RFC 7307 made LDP set up unicast LSPs along MT routing paths.

The Flexible Algorithm (FA, RFC 9350) is a lighter way to carve a sub-topology out of a topology using constraints and a computation algorithm. This document calls the general idea the IGP Algorithm (IPA), an 8-bit identifier, because other algorithms might be defined later.

Multipoint LDP (mLDP, RFC 6388) builds point-to-multipoint (P2MP) and multipoint-to-multipoint (MP2MP) LSPs. To work in an MTR or FA network it must become topology and algorithm aware, so the topology identifier becomes the 2-tuple {MTR Topology Id, IPA}.
sections.plainLanguage: Some roads are only for buses and some only for bikes. The delivery system for many-viewer streams has to learn which map to use.

sections.title: Making the Topology Part of the FEC
sections.content:
The MT-ID already identifies an MTR topology in an LSP's FEC. To avoid conflicting policies for the same mLDP FEC, the MT-ID must be part of the FEC, so different MT-ID values give unique MP-LSP FEC elements. The same holds for the IPA, which also tells each hop which algorithm to use to build the LSP.

Because the tuple is part of the FEC, it applies to every LDP message that may carry an mLDP FEC element. The tuple says in which (sub-)topology the root address of the MP LSP must be resolved, so it is encoded as part of the root address.
sections.plainLanguage: Writing the map name on the delivery label means two deliveries to the same place on different maps never get mixed up.

sections.title: MT IP Address Families and the MT MP FEC Element
sections.content:
RFC 7307 defined the address families MT IP and MT IPv6. Here, 8 bits of the 16-bit Reserved field are used to carry the IPA. The Reserved bits that remain MUST be zero on transmission and MUST be ignored on receipt. After the address come the Reserved byte, the IPA byte and the MT-ID.

The MT-scoped MP FEC element uses this extended address family for the root node address, followed by the usual opaque length and value. It applies to the P2MP (type 0x6), MP2MP-up (type 0x7) and MP2MP-down (type 0x8) elements, and to the Typed Wildcard FEC Element (type 0x5), whose element type MUST then be one of those MP FECs.

For the BGP PMSI tunnel attribute of RFC 6514, the MT-scoped form of the P2MP or MP2MP FEC element MUST be used as the Tunnel Identifier when this extension is in use.
sections.plainLanguage: The address on the label gets two extra boxes: one for the map and one for the way of drawing it.

sections.title: The MT Multipoint Capability
sections.content:
Support is announced with a new LDP capability, MT Multipoint, defined under the guidelines of RFC 5561. A speaker MAY send it in an Initialization message at session setup, or later in a Capability message if the Dynamic Announcement capability was negotiated.

In the TLV, the U and F bits MUST be 1 and 0, the Length MUST be 1 because no capability-specific data follows, and the S bit is 1 to announce or 0 to withdraw. A speaker that has advertised and negotiated it MUST support topology-scoped mLDP FECs in LDP messages and topology-scoped forwarding setup.
sections.plainLanguage: Before swapping maps, two neighbours say "I can read the special maps too".

sections.title: Wildcards, End-of-LIB and Path Selection
sections.content:
The Typed Wildcard FEC procedures of RFC 5918 apply as is. The MT extensions allow MT IP or MT IPv6 in the Address Family field of a Typed Wildcard MP FEC Element, so wildcard operations can be scoped to one (sub-)topology. End-of-LIB (RFC 5919) also needs no change, so a speaker MAY signal convergence per (sub-)topology.

mLDP needs no separate forwarding tables per topology, because each MP LSP is unique through the tuple in its FEC and has its own local label. What changes are two selection steps:

  • Upstream LSR selection: the tuple chooses the (sub-)topology used to find the best path to the root, and the next hop of that path picks the LDP peer as in RFC 6388.
  • Downstream interface selection: an interface may only be chosen if it is part of the same (sub-)topology signaled in the FEC element.
sections.plainLanguage: Each delivery truck only drives on roads from its own map, both when picking who to ask and where to send things on.

sections.title: LSP Ping for MT Paths
sections.content:
RFC 6425 defines LSP ping sub-TLVs for multipoint LDP FECs, carried in the Target FEC Stack TLV of an MPLS Echo Request (RFC 8029). For MT MP LSPs the existing P2MP and MP2MP LDP FEC Stack sub-types are reused, with MT IP or MT IPv6 in the Address Family field and the Address Length set to 8 or 20 respectively.

The {MT-ID, IPA} information extends the Root LSR Address field. The procedures are otherwise those of RFC 6425; the only difference is that the root address is now (sub-)topology scoped.
sections.plainLanguage: A test message can check the path too, as long as it says which map it is travelling on.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The extension introduces no new security considerations beyond those of base LDP (RFC 5036), LDP Multi-Topology (RFC 7307), base mLDP (RFC 6388) and the MPLS security framework (RFC 5920).

IANA assigned the value 0x0510 for the MT Multipoint Capability in the TLV Type Name Space registry of the Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) Parameters group.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing new to worry about beyond the old rules, and one new number was reserved for the new feature.
